It was a great ride, but now that there is about 3 months until the puck drops on opening night, we have to fill the void that hockey has left behind. What do you think the future holds for the Lightning in the short and long term? Who are the 'core' group of players that think will stick around? Palat, Johnson, Kuch, Stamkos, Hedman, Killhorny?

It's an interesting discussion in net with Bish and Vasy. Does Bish stick around after the next two years? Does Vasy take his spot as the #1 over the course of the next two seasons?

Drouin should get a legitimate chance to play alongside Stamkos on the top line this season. It's becoming a problem for the franchise, a good problem at that, but a problem nonetheless. A glut of top six forwards in the system that are pressing for playing time. Vladdy, Drouin, Callahan, Val Fil, the triplets, Killorn, and there are more coming with guys like Peca and Point specifically. It's starting to get into a longjam of skill forwards that hopefully will be sorted out well enough -- but who stays and goes?

The same thing is happening on the defensive back end. Koekkoek and Deangelo will soon transition to the pro game, and I really like the strides that Nesterov is making. The Hedman/Stralman combo at the top is outstanding and guaranteed to be here for some years, but after that, it gets interesting.

Definitely a really bright future for many years. If Yzerman and the scouting department keep an eye for developing talent within the system and execute, it might be a different experience for fans as players outside of Stamkos/Hedman and maybe Johnson/Kucherov could be shown the door for younger, and more importantly significantly cheaper, talent.

Minecraft. Although I don't play it much anymore, I loved all the things I could do in it. From the moment I built my first house, I was hooked. I particularly loved the community. People made so many amazing buildings and awesome new mods to try out. My friends and I ran a server and we had an amazing time playing together. I remember the times where we would intentionally crash the server by blowing up a ton of TNT and laughing hysterically at it. My brother had a save file as adult link and I just used to mess about on there. Skip years later and I attempt to complete the game. Reach water temple and BAM, there was a block blocking me and I couldn't get through. I tried everything, I got frustrated then just messed about in hyrule field. Was too scared to play again, dat eerie music.. Also it took me ages to get to that point so to do "another" play through would be annoying.

Atm, I'm waiting for the oot HD texture pack to be completed, the game just doesn't look as good as it did.

The crucial thing about the Water Temple, I think, is whether you get lucky with it the first time you play through it. By this I mean whether you, by chance, happen to make the right choices of where to go from the very beginning, so that you actually beat the dungeon without realising how unlinear it is and how a single wrong turn can lead you into an almost inescapable knot of confusion. The people who got lucky are the ones who finished the game and then were confident enough to replay it and explore further. Those unlucky ones are the ones like our friend here who was stuck for years. And it only makes it all worse that this was on the pre-internet and pre-walkthrough area.

In my case, I got lucky. And it also helped that I was playing it with a bunch of other kids, which somehow does help when figuring out difficult games.

So many guilds to join and secrets to find. Even today, the story and world-building aspect holds up even if the graphics and the gameplay are quite dated.

I'm glad it didn't bother you as much as it did me, but even when they were reminiscing about that time in Luca, they cut the audio for it-- pretty telling!

I think they cut the audio because they wanted to preserve the nostalgia of when you visited Luca without juxtaposing an awkward laugh in there, not because they thought the scene was poorly done. The scene is meant to be awkward and embarrassing, just like when Cloud puts a dress on and gets hit on by Don Corneo. I think once the FF7 remake comes out, if we get a remake of those particular crossdressing scenes, then people are going to react the same way as they did to the laughing scene. Voice acting plays a major part in how we react to cutscenes.

Excellent point, and can't really argue anything against it-- I guess it was just that remembering the scene was a little off putting seeing as there's a lot of stigma attached to it.

Wakka even goes ahead and pokes fun of them after the scene, so it just further proves your point.

Of all time? That's a pretty tough choice.

But I think I'd have to go with Shattered Galaxy. It's an MMORTS I haven't seen any Western developer try successfully, and even Shattered Galaxy was fairly niche. It has since died due to the company behind it not doing anything. End of Nations was something similar, but it turned out Trion had no fucking clue what they were doing.

Here's a single battle. Basically it had a single server with 80 different maps that were being fought over 24/7. Each player controls a single squad of units, ranging from 6-12 depending on how you leveled your commander. Each unit in each squad was fully customizable. 3 factions, as well as a "mercenary" option. Each map had 1-5 contention points. Some maps required all contention points to be won. Others required a majority.Game even had a damned political system.

There were options for everyone. Nukes, tanks, snipers, bombers, medics, teleporters, catapults, stealth, infantry, and even alien life forms were all usable units. I miss that damn game; which for some reason is still up and running. Most of the map has been taken over by the Alien AI that invades if maps aren't fought over after a while now.

I hate to admit it after being a dedicated Half-Life and CoD player for many years, but it's Skyrim. I watched my son playing Morrowind and Skyrim on the Xbox. I wound up buying the Legendary Edition of Skyrim for the Xbox, and I was quickly hooked. It's been the single most addictive game I've played, maybe because I loved the paper and pencil RPG game Dungeons & Dragons so much as a young man in the early 80s. Skyrim seemed so reminiscent of that experience, so immersive compared to most other FPS games I've played over the years. I play now on an underpowered laptop so I can use some weapon and gameplay mods, and I love it. I've been playing less than a year, and I've got over 1500 hours between the Xbox and Steam. For whatever reason, it just never, ever seems to get old for me. My dream is to be able to afford a decent gaming laptop so I'll be able to play Skyrim at more than 20 frames per second. Still, it's a joy for me that way, discovering locations, NPCs, monsters, and following quests, at a frame rate that would be totally unacceptable for any other game.

Friggin', Morrowind. The new TES games are so watered down. When I learned that Skyrim had no spellmaking and had such a small amount of spells I was really disappointed. The game's spell system and enchanting system really made the game for me. There's nothing like making a huge area fire spell and raining down meteors from the top of your Telvanni tower. I once made a dagger that summoned a flame Atronach every time it hit. And don't even get me started on the lore. The first stupid tiny port town that you visit has so much world-building in it. From letters and clues around town you uncover a story of guard corruption in Seyda Neen, and that's just a tiny city! There's a city called Vivec that's literally 9 Solitudes large. Including a temple and an asteroid moon prison/guard tower. There was so much love and passion put into that game that I didn't see from casual af Skyrim and Oblivion. I've seen people who won't play it because it "looks old." Well, take it from me, a randy on the internet, that it's worth it. And it's great.
